Theneuropeptideoxytocin(OT)playsacriticalroleinsocialprocesses1 .IntranasalOTadministrationinhealthy people impacts mentalizing2 , empathy3 , trust4 , biological motion detection5 , and emotion recognition6 . Genetic polymorphisms on the oxytocin receptor gene may confer cumulative risk for social impairment7 . Thus, OT is a candidate system for involvement in disorders that feature core social impairments, such as autism spectrum disorder(ASD).Severalsingle-administrationstudiesindicatethatindividualswithASDdemonstrateshort-term symptom improvement following OT inhalation8–11 ; however, chronic administration studies are few and show mixed effects. Initial attempts revealed only modest improvements in primary outcome measures12,13 , although more recent studies show enhancement in social responsiveness in children14 as well as social reciprocity in adults15 . Our understanding of the potential for OT to treat ASD is hampered by a lack of sensitive, objective measures that are designed to illuminate mechanisms of change. dose.text: Older participants (aged 16–19 y) received a dose of 24 IU (two puffs per nostril), in accordance with most studies of intranasal OT in adults71.
Twelve- to 15-y-olds received 75% of the adult dose or 18 IU (three puffs overall).
The youngest age group (aged 7–11 y) received 50% of the typical adult dose (12 IU or one puff per nostril).
